books.title: A Caricature of Marxism and Imperialist Economism
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Lenin's polemic against 'imperialist economism', refuting the dogma that finance capital makes democratic demands, national self-determination, and anti-colonial liberation impossible or obsolete.
books.subject: Imperialism and National Self-Determination

books.title: A Characterisation of Economic Romanticism
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Lenin's comprehensive critique of Sismondi and Russian Narodism, dismantling petty-bourgeois romantic economics and demonstrating how capitalism develops the home market through the ruination of subsistence producers.
books.subject: Political Economy and Critique of Romanticism

books.title: A United Front Against Debt
books.author: Thomas Sankara
books.shortDescription: Delivered in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, on July 29, 1987, at the summit of the Organization of African Unity, this landmark speech by Captain Thomas Sankara calls for a continental refusal to pay foreign debt, exposing sovereign debt as an instrument of neocolonial reconquest.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Analysis of the Classes in Chinese Society
books.author: Mao Zedong
books.shortDescription: Written in March 1926 as the opening essay of Volume I of the Selected Works of Mao Zedong, Analysis of the Classes in Chinese Society poses the famous strategic question: 'Who are our enemies? Who are our friends?' Written to combat both Chen Duxiu's Right opportunism and Zhang Guotao's 'Left' opportunism, Mao conducts a concrete materialist class analysis of semi-colonial, semi-feudal China, identifying the industrial proletariat as the leading force and the vast semi-proletarian peasantry as its closest revolutionary ally.
books.subject: Class Struggle

books.title: Anarchism or Socialism?
books.author: Joseph Stalin
books.shortDescription: Written between December 1906 and January 1907 as a series of articles in Georgian socialist periodicals, Anarchism or Socialism? is Stalin's early philosophical defense of dialectical and historical materialism against the Georgian anarchists following Prince Kropotkin. The treatise contrasts the materialist foundation of scientific socialism with individualist anarchist philosophy, demonstrating that individual liberation is impossible without the collective emancipation of the working class.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Blacks Must Take Responsibility for Their Own History
books.author: Thomas Sankara
books.shortDescription: Delivered in Ouagadougou on April 21, 1986, at the opening of the International Symposium for the Creation of the Black Institute (Institut des peuples noirs), this speech by Captain Thomas Sankara honors historian Cheikh Anta Diop and outlines a Pan-African framework for cultural decolonization, historical agency, and global solidarity.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Blancism
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Published in Pravda No. 27 on April 8 (21), 1917, shortly after Lenin's return to Petrograd and the presentation of his April Theses, this article exposes the Menshevik and Socialist-Revolutionary leadership of the Soviets for repeating the tragic class-collaborationist illusions of the French reformist Louis Blanc in 1848.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Capitalism and Female Labour
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written on April 27, 1913, and published in Pravda on May 5, 1913, this brief article addresses an exhibition in Paris showcasing the horrific wage exploitation of women engaged in domestic sweatshop piecework. Lenin utilizes this data to unmask the systematic roots of working-class female oppression under capitalism.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: The Civil War in France
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Written by Karl Marx between April and May 1871 as an official address to the General Council of the International Workingmen's Association, The Civil War in France is Marx's seminal historical materialist analysis of the Paris Commune. Written while Communards were defending Paris against Versaillist troops, Marx synthesizes the lessons of the first working-class government in history, establishing the core Marxist proposition that the working class cannot simply lay hold of the ready-made state machinery and wield it for its own purposes, but must smash the bourgeois state apparatus and replace it with genuine proletarian democracy.
books.subject: State Theory and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

books.title: Communism and the Family
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: First published in 1920 during the Russian Civil War, Communism and the Family is Alexandra Kollontai's landmark pamphlet on Marxist feminism and social transformation. Kollontai demonstrates how industrial capitalism destroyed the self-contained domestic economy, pulling women into wage labor while leaving them burdened with unpaid housework. She outlines how a socialist society replaces private domestic isolation with collective kitchens, laundries, and communal childcare, liberating women to participate fully in economic and political life as equal human beings.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: The Communist Manifesto
books.author: Karl Marx & Friedrich Engels
books.shortDescription: Commissioned by the Communist League and published in London in February 1848, this pamphlet was written during a period of massive political unrest across Europe. It explains the class struggle and critiques capitalism, serving as a call to action for the working class.
books.subject: Class Struggle

books.title: Capital: Volume 1 (The Process of Production of Capital)
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: First published in 1867, Volume 1 of Marx's magnum opus analyzes the capitalist mode of production, commodity fetishism, surplus value, wage labor, and primitive accumulation.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: Capital: Volume 2 (The Process of Circulation of Capital)
books.author: Karl Marx (ed. Friedrich Engels)
books.shortDescription: Edited by Friedrich Engels and published posthumously in 1885, Volume 2 examines the circulation of capital, turnover times, reproduction schemes, and macro-economic circuit dynamics.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: Capital: Volume 3 (The Process of Capitalist Production as a Whole)
books.author: Karl Marx (ed. Friedrich Engels)
books.shortDescription: Published in 1894 by Engels, Volume 3 synthesizes production and circulation to explain profit equalization, the tendency of the rate of profit to fall, credit, fictitious capital, and ground rent.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: The Foundations of Leninism
books.author: Joseph Stalin
books.shortDescription: Delivered as a series of lectures at Sverdlov University in Moscow in April 1924 shortly after Lenin's death, The Foundations of Leninism systematically codifies and synthesizes Lenin's theoretical and practical contributions to Marxism. Stalin defines Leninism as 'Marxism of the era of imperialism and the proletarian revolution,' formulating core principles of the vanguard party, democratic centralism, the worker-peasant alliance, and the dictatorship of the proletariat.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Critique of the Gotha Programme
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Written by Karl Marx in 1875 as marginal notes on the draft program of the united German Social Democratic Workers' Party, this seminal text details the transition from capitalism to lower and higher phases of communist society.
books.subject: Classical Marxism

books.title: Grundrisse
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Written in 1857-1858, the Grundrisse (German for 'Outlines') is a massive set of raw, private notebooks where Marx worked out his economic theories before writing Capital. Left unpublished until 1939, it contains Marx's most futuristic speculations on automation, technology, and the liberation of human free time.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: On Guerrilla Warfare
books.author: Mao Zedong
books.shortDescription: First published in 1937 during the Second Sino-Japanese War while Mao Zedong was based in Yan'an, this seminal treatise outlines the military and political doctrine of protracted guerrilla warfare. Mao establishes that guerrilla warfare is not merely a military tactic, but a political struggle of the masses against a foreign invader or oppressive ruling class, requiring deep integration with the population.
books.subject: Anti-Imperialism

books.title: Guerrilla Warfare: A Method
books.author: Che Guevara
books.shortDescription: Published in September 1963 in the theoretical journal Cuba Socialista, this seminal essay by Ernesto 'Che' Guevara synthesizes the military, political, and economic principles of the Cuban Revolution into a strategic method for continental anti-imperialist struggle in Latin America and the Global South. Guevara establishes that guerrilla warfare is a political weapon aimed at the conquest of state power, requiring the mobilization of the peasant masses and the creation of subjective revolutionary consciousness.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: How the Capitalists Are Trying to Scare the People
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Published in Pravda No. 61 on June 1 (May 19), 1917, during the revolutionary dual-power crisis in Russia, this polemic refutes an editorial from the bourgeois capitalist journal Finansovaya Gazeta, which attempted to terrify the public into opposing workers' control over industry.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Notes for the Study of the Ideology of the Cuban Revolution
books.author: Che Guevara
books.shortDescription: Published in Verde Olivo on October 8, 1960, during the initial consolidation of revolutionary state power in Cuba, this seminal essay articulates the organic Marxist character of the Cuban Revolution and outlines the transformation of revolutionary fighters through practical struggle alongside the peasantry.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written in Zurich in early 1916, during World War I, and first published as a pamphlet in mid-1917 in Petrograd. Lenin wrote it under tsarist censorship, forcing him to use cautious, 'Aesopian' language and focus on purely economic analysis. The work builds on J.A. Hobson's and Rudolf Hilferding's studies of imperialism and finance capital, synthesising their data into a Marxist framework that explains imperialism as a necessary stage of capitalist development, not merely a policy choice.
books.subject: Anti-Imperialism

books.title: Imperialism and World Economy
books.author: Nikolai Bukharin
books.shortDescription: Written in 1915 during World War I with an introduction by V.I. Lenin and published in 1917, Imperialism and World Economy is Nikolai Bukharin's landmark Marxist study of global monopoly capitalism. Bukharin analyzes the dual dialectical process of the internationalization of economic life and the nationalization (statification) of capital into competing 'state-capitalist trusts', demonstrating why monopoly competition inevitably escalates from protective tariffs and capital export into militarism and world war.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: “Left-Wing” Childishness and the Petty-Bourgeois Mentality
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written in May 1918 during the fierce debate over the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk and Soviet economic policy, V.I. Lenin replies to the 'Left Communist' faction (including Nikolai Bukharin, Valerian Osinsky, and Karl Radek) and their journal Kommunist. Lenin exposes how ultra-left revolutionary phrase-making masks petty-bourgeois vacillation and a failure to grasp the concrete material tasks of transitioning from capitalism to socialism.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: “Left-Wing” Communism: an Infantile Disorder
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written in 1920 for the Second Congress of the Communist International, Lenin's classic treatise critiques sectarian 'left' radicalism and outlines pragmatic, principled revolutionary strategy and tactics.
books.subject: Party Strategy and Tactics

books.title: Lenin on the Women's Question
books.author: Clara Zetkin
books.shortDescription: Recorded by German Marxist theorist and communist leader Clara Zetkin in the autumn of 1920 in the Kremlin, Lenin on the Women's Question preserves her famous conversation with V.I. Lenin on the foundations of the international communist women's movement. Together they analyze why true female emancipation is inseparable from the abolition of private property, critique bourgeois feminism and individualistic sexual theories, and outline the material socialization of domestic housework and childcare in Soviet Russia.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: Materialism and Empirio-criticism
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written by Lenin between February and October 1908 during his Geneva exile following the defeat of the 1905 Russian Revolution, this major philosophical work combats subjective idealist and neo-Kantian tendencies (Machism, Empirio-criticism, and Bogadanov's Empirio-monism) that infected the Russian Social-Democratic party under the guise of 'modernizing' Marxism with contemporary physics.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Mobilising the Masses for the Invasion
books.author: Che Guevara
books.shortDescription: Delivered to sugar workers in Santa Clara on March 28, 1961, merely twenty days before the CIA-sponsored Bay of Pigs invasion (Playa Girón), this speech prepares the Cuban working class for imminent imperialist military aggression and outlines the necessity of unyielding national resistance.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: On Contradiction
books.author: Mao Zedong
books.shortDescription: A simplified guide to Mao Zedong's essay on how conflict and change work. It explains why opposing forces exist in everything and how focusing on the main problem helps solve real-life challenges.
books.subject: Dialectics

books.title: On Practice
books.author: Mao Zedong
books.shortDescription: Delivered in July 1937 as a lecture at the Anti-Japanese Military and Political College in Yan'an alongside On Contradiction, On Practice: On the Relation Between Knowledge and Practice, Between Knowing and Doing is Mao Zedong's classic treatise on the Marxist theory of knowledge (epistemology). Written to combat both dogmatism and empiricism inside the Communist Party, Mao explains how human knowledge arises from social practice (production, class struggle, and scientific experiment), leaps from perceptual to rational knowledge, and returns to revolutionary practice to change the world.
books.subject: Dialectical Materialism

books.title: On Protracted War
books.author: Mao Zedong
books.shortDescription: Mao's classic 1938 lectures applying materialist dialectics to the War of Resistance Against Japan, refuting both defeatism and quick-victory illusions while outlining the three stages of protracted people's war.
books.subject: Anti-Imperialism and Military Strategy

books.title: On Revolutionary Medicine
books.author: Che Guevara
books.shortDescription: Delivered on August 19, 1960, to the Cuban Militia, this speech traces Che's personal transition from an individual medical doctor traveling Latin America into a revolutionary combatant, laying the theoretical foundation for universal socialist healthcare and socialized medicine.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People
books.author: Mao Zedong
books.shortDescription: Mao's landmark 1957 speech distinguishing antagonistic contradictions between the people and the enemy from non-antagonistic contradictions among the people under socialism.
books.subject: Dialectics and Socialist Construction

books.title: The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State
books.author: Friedrich Engels
books.shortDescription: Published in 1884 following Karl Marx's death, this landmark work draws on Lewis H. Morgan's anthropological research into Indigenous societies to demonstrate that social institutions like the monogamous family, private property, and the state are not eternal features of human existence, but historical developments that arose alongside class division.
books.subject: Anthropology

books.title: Our Revolution
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Dictated on January 16 and 17, 1923, during Lenin's final illness, this brief masterpiece critiques Menshevik memoirist Nikolai Sukhanov and the reformists of the Second International for their mechanical, pedantic misunderstanding of historical materialism and the dialectics of world revolution.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: The Principles of Communism
books.author: Friedrich Engels
books.shortDescription: Drafted by Friedrich Engels in 1847 as a 25-question catechism for the Communist League, this foundational work provides clear, accessible answers explaining the core principles of Marxism.
books.subject: Classical Marxism

books.title: Prostitution and Ways of Fighting It
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: Delivered as a speech to the Third All-Russian Conference of Heads of Regional Women's Departments in 1921, Prostitution and Ways of Fighting It is Alexandra Kollontai's groundbreaking Marxist analysis of sex work and Soviet social policy. Kollontai argues that prostitution is rooted in capitalist poverty and female economic dependence, defining prostitutes not as criminals or fallen women, but as labor deserters alongside non-working kept wives. She outlines Soviet strategies to eradicate prostitution through vocational training, economic equality, public health, and free comradeship.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: Red Love
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: Published in 1927, Red Love (Vasilisa Malygina) is Alexandra Kollontai's pioneering revolutionary novel set during the New Economic Policy (NEP) in Soviet Russia. The novel dramatizes the conflict between the new communist morality of female economic independence and the revival of bourgeois careerism and possessiveness. Following Vasilisa, a devoted Bolshevik textile worker, the narrative explores the breakdown of her marriage to Volodya as he succumbs to NEP-era bureaucratization and bourgeois corruption, illustrating the necessity for working women to build self-reliance through socialized labor and revolutionary comradeship.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: Reform or Revolution
books.author: Rosa Luxemburg
books.shortDescription: First published in 1899-1900 as a polemic against Eduard Bernstein's revisionist reformism, Social Reform or Revolution is Rosa Luxemburg's masterwork defending scientific socialism. Luxemburg demonstrates that trade unions and legislative reforms cannot gradually dissolve capitalist exploitation, proving that reform and revolution are not optional pathways to the same goal, but fundamental choices between repairing capitalism or abolishing wage slavery.
books.subject: Marxist Political Economy

books.title: Sexual Relations and the Class Struggle
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: Written in 1921, Sexual Relations and the Class Struggle is Alexandra Kollontai's foundational theoretical essay applying historical materialism to sexual morality, marriage, and human psychology. Kollontai demonstrates how sexual ethics evolve alongside economic modes of production, tracing the transition from feudal tribalism to bourgeois individualistic possessiveness. She argues that capitalist atomization produces acute spiritual loneliness and possessive marital rights, urging the revolutionary working class to forge a new sexual code based on comradely solidarity, female independence, and collective class unity.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: The Social Basis of the Woman Question
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: First published in 1909, The Social Basis of the Woman Question is Alexandra Kollontai's landmark text drawing a sharp materialist distinction between bourgeois feminism and proletarian women's liberation. Kollontai demonstrates that while bourgeois feminists seek equal privileges with men within the existing capitalist framework, working women seek to abolish economic slavery alongside male comrades through socialized labor, universal childcare, and revolutionary transformation.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: Socialism and Anarchism
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Published in Novaya Zhizn on November 25, 1905, during the First Russian Revolution, this article evaluates the decision of the St. Petersburg Soviet of Workers' Deputies to reject an application by anarchists for representation, explaining the fundamental theoretical and tactical divide separating scientific socialism from anarchism.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Socialism and Man in Cuba
books.author: Che Guevara
books.shortDescription: Written in March 1965 as an open letter to Carlos Quijano, editor of the Uruguayan weekly Marcha, this text constitutes Che Guevara's most famous and comprehensive theoretical statement on the human dimension of socialist construction, the ethics of the vanguard, moral incentives, and the creation of the New Man and Woman.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Socialism and Religion
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Published in Novaya Zhizn in December 1905 during the high tide of the First Russian Revolution, this classic article outlines the Marxist perspective on religious belief, state secularism, and working-class party organization.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Socialism and War
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Lenin's decisive polemic defining the Marxist stance on World War I, contrasting revolutionary internationalism and defeatism against bourgeois pacifism and social-chauvinist betrayal.
books.subject: Imperialism, War and Internationalism

books.title: Society of the Future
books.author: August Bebel
books.shortDescription: Published as a standalone edition of Part III ('The Socialisation of Society') of August Bebel's classic Woman and Socialism (1879), Society of the Future presents one of the most detailed and inspiring Marxist visions of how a post-capitalist socialist commonwealth will organize production, agriculture, education, art, domestic life, and international relations.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Soviet Power and the Status of Women
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Published in Pravda on November 6, 1919, to commemorate the second anniversary of the October Revolution during the height of the Russian Civil War and imperialist intervention, this article evaluates the profound legal, social, and economic strides taken by the Soviet Republic to abolish sex inequalities and domestic servitude.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Summary of Dialectics
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written between 1914 and 1915 in Bern, Switzerland, following the outbreak of World War I and the collapse of the Second International, these philosophical notebooks record Lenin's deep study of Hegel's Science of Logic, formulating the 16 elements of dialectics and the famous fragment 'On the Question of Dialectics'.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: The Attitude of the Workers' Party to Religion
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Published in Proletary in May 1909 during a period of reaction following the defeat of the 1905 Russian Revolution, The Attitude of the Workers' Party to Religion is V.I. Lenin's classic treatise on dialectical materialism and religious policy. Lenin addresses debates in the Russian Duma and within the Bolshevik party, explaining why Marxists are absolute philosophical materialists yet oppose anarchistic declarations of war on religion, insisting that atheist education must be subordinated to the practical class struggle.
books.subject: Marxist Philosophy and Party Strategy

books.title: The Bolsheviks and the Petty Bourgeoisie
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Published in Novy Luch on February 25, 1907, during the elections to the Second State Duma, this polemical article analyzes class differentiation in the Russian Revolution of 1905 to 1907. Responding to the Trudovik organ Noviye Sily, Lenin dissects the social character of the Constitutional-Democratic Party (Cadets) and refutes Menshevik arguments regarding alliances with liberal reformists.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: The Courage to Criticize Imperialism
books.author: Thomas Sankara
books.shortDescription: Conducted in January 1987 by TASS special envoy Boris Chabaev following the 1986 Reykjavik summit between Mikhail Gorbachev and Ronald Reagan, this interview presents Captain Thomas Sankara’s vision of Pan-African anti-imperialism, global disarmament, and national sovereignty for Burkina Faso and the Global South.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: A Great Love
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: First published in 1929, A Great Love is Alexandra Kollontai's acclaimed collection of three novellas: A Great Love, Sisters, and The Loves of Three Generations. Through intimate narrative studies of Bolshevik revolutionaries, working mothers, and changing familial standards, Kollontai explores the psychological dilemmas facing women during the transition to socialism. The title story dramatizes the emotional friction between a devoted female organizer and her male comrade, while Sisters and Three Generations examine workplace exploitation, single motherhood, and the evolution of sexual morality across successive generations.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: The Holy Family
books.author: Karl Marx & Friedrich Engels
books.shortDescription: Published in 1845, The Holy Family, or Critique of Critical Critique was the first major collaborative work by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. Written as a polemic against Bruno Bauer and the Young Hegelian 'Critical Critics', the text marks a decisive turning point in the development of scientific socialism. Marx and Engels demolish speculative Hegelian idealism, formulate the historic mission of the proletariat to abolish private property, trace the philosophical roots of socialism to 18th-century French materialism, and establish Charles Fourier's principle that women's emancipation is the natural measure of general social freedom.
books.subject: Marxist Philosophy and Historical Materialism

books.title: The Revolutionary Proletariat and the Right of Nations to Self-Determination
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Written in German in October 1915 in response to Karl Radek's article in Berner Tagwacht following the Zimmerwald Conference, this essay presents Lenin's foundational formulation of the national question during the imperialist world war, linking democratic self-determination to socialist revolution.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: The State and Revolution
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Lenin's foundational treatise on Marxist state theory, detailing the dictatorship of the proletariat, the smashing of the bourgeois state machine, and the economic basis for the withering away of the state.
books.subject: State Theory and Revolution

books.title: Fascism
books.author: Clara Zetkin
books.shortDescription: Published in Labour Monthly in August 1923 following her landmark June 1923 address to the Enlarged Executive Committee of the Communist International, Fascism is Clara Zetkin's foundational materialist analysis of the rise of Italian and German fascism. Written less than a year after Mussolini's March on Rome, Zetkin dissects how decaying capitalism and social-democratic betrayal enabled fascism to mobilize ruined petty-bourgeois layers and disillusioned workers behind pseudo-revolutionary demagogy while serving heavy industry and finance capital.
books.subject: Fascism Analysis

books.title: The Trade Unions, The Present Situation and Trotsky’s Mistakes
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Lenin's famous 1920 speech analyzing the role of trade unions under the dictatorship of the proletariat as schools of communism, refuting Trotsky's proposals for administrative incorporation.
books.subject: Trade Unions and Socialist Transition

books.title: Theses on Communist Morality in the Sphere of Marital Relations
books.author: Alexandra Kollontai
books.shortDescription: First published in Kommunistka (No. 12, 1921), Theses on Communist Morality in the Sphere of Marital Relations presents Alexandra Kollontai's definitive guidelines for revolutionary personal ethics. Kollontai demonstrates that as the workers' state assumes responsibility for public dining, laundries, and child welfare, human relationships are liberated from economic dependence, proprietary jealousy, and commercial marriage contracts, enabling true emotional solidarity.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism

books.title: Value, Price and Profit
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: First published in 1865, this text forms an essential part of Karl Marx's critique of political economy. It provides simplified, yet rigorous, explanations of key capitalist economic concepts.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: Wage Labour and Capital
books.author: Karl Marx
books.shortDescription: Based on lectures Marx delivered in 1847 to the German Workingmen's Club in Brussels, this work provides a straightforward and accessible explanation of the economic relationships under capitalism, particularly how labor becomes a commodity and how wages are determined.
books.subject: Political Economy

books.title: What Is To Be Done?
books.author: V.I. Lenin
books.shortDescription: Lenin's seminal work on political organization, arguing that working-class political consciousness requires systematic theoretical education rather than pure trade unionism.
books.subject: Party Organization

books.title: Woman and Socialism
books.author: August Bebel
books.shortDescription: First published illegally in 1879 under Bismarck's Anti-Socialist Laws and expanded through fifty editions, Woman and Socialism by August Bebel was the foundational Marxist text on women's liberation and socialist reconstruction. Structured in three parts (Woman in the Past, Woman at the Present Day, and The Socialisation of Society), Bebel applies historical materialism to trace women's oppression from the overthrow of primeval maternal law through modern capitalism, demonstrating that the emancipation of women is inseparable from the overthrow of wage slavery.
books.subject: Theory and Philosophy

books.title: Women's Suffrage and Class Struggle
books.author: Rosa Luxemburg
books.shortDescription: Delivered at the Second Social Democratic Women's Rally in Stuttgart, Germany on May 12, 1912, Women's Suffrage and Class Struggle is Rosa Luxemburg's classic speech demonstrating why working-class women's vote is a revolutionary threat to the capitalist state. Luxemburg contrasts working women—who create capitalist surplus value in factories and farms—with bourgeois women who act as co-consumers of surplus value, proving that the struggle for women's suffrage is an integral part of the proletarian revolution.
books.subject: Marxist Feminism
